paragraphs.en: Our teacher, Miss Chevalier, was a {small} {woman} with a moon face, {fatty} fingers and {curl} that sprang {straight} up from her head, {hence} the {funny} {name} “Poodle（卷毛狗）”.She taught in our reading {club}.Sometimes she would look in and ask what we were reading—not to check but to know.
paragraphs.cn: 我们的老师谢瓦利埃小姐是个身材矮 <u> 小的女人 </u> ，长着一张圆脸， <u> 胖乎乎的 </u> 手指，还有从头顶 <u> 直接 </u> 向上 <u> 翘 </u> 起的 <u> 卷发 </u> ， <u> 因此 </u> 得了“卷毛狗”这个 <u> 有趣的绰号 </u> 。她在我们读书 <u> 俱乐部 </u> 任教。有时她会进来看看，问问我们正在读什么——不是为了检查，而是为了了解。

paragraphs.en: That's what happened the {day} my club was reading aloud a {poem} by Henry Longfellow. I guess I was better than the others, for Miss Chevalier asked a while {later},“Addie, I was {wonder} if you would {recite} the whole poem to the Saturday evening's club.”She said a {famous} professor was going to give a lecture about the {poet}, and a {presentation} of that poem would be a fresh way to start.
paragraphs.cn: 那是我们俱乐部正在大声朗读亨利·朗费罗的一首 <u> 诗 </u> 的那 <u> 天 </u> 发生的事。我猜想我读得比别人好，因为 <u> 过了 </u> 一会儿，谢瓦利埃老师问我：“艾迪，我在 <u> 想 </u> 你是否愿意为周六晚上的俱乐部 <u> 朗诵 </u> 整首诗。”她说有一位 <u> 知名 </u> 教授要做关于这位 <u> 诗人 </u> 的演讲，而 <u> 展示 </u> 这首诗将是一个新颖的开场方式。

paragraphs.en: She asked me to {memorize} it.“But that shouldn't be a problem for a {child} of your ability,”she added.I'm telling you, my happy feet {barely} {touch} the {ground} all the way home.To me, that was the biggest thing ever and I soon {learn} the whole poem by {heart}, well prepared for our first {rehearsal}.
paragraphs.cn: 她让我把诗 <u> 背下来 </u> ，并且补充道：“不过，对于像你这样有能力的 <u> 孩子 </u> 来说，这应该不成问题。”说真的，回家的路上，我高兴得脚 <u> 几乎没沾 </u> 过 <u> 地 </u> 。对我来说，这是有史以来最重要的事，我很快就把整首诗熟 <u> 记 </u> 于 <u> 心 </u> 了，为我们的第一次 <u> 排练 </u> 做好了充分准备。

paragraphs.en: I was {desperately} nervous when I went to her {office} the {next} day.But the {good} {thing} was she always had the smile that would make you feel like you just did something right.
paragraphs.cn: <u> 第二 </u> 天去她 <u> 办公室 </u> 的时候，我紧张得 <u> 要命 </u> 。但 <u> 好在 </u> 她总是面带微笑，让你觉得自己刚刚做了一件正确的事。

paragraphs.en: {halfway} through the poem, Miss Chevalier {stop} me and asked if I knew what “impetuous” meant. {despite} her {encouraging} smile, I wanted to {sink} through the {floor} because I was {unsure} about its {pronunciation} as well as its {meaning}.Miss Chevalier {pretend} not to have {notice} my {red} face and {hand} me a dictionary, asking me to read its {definition} {aloud} .“Impetuous has two definitions: {rush} with great {force} or {violence}; acting suddenly, with {little} thought.”
paragraphs.cn: 诗背到 <u> 一半 </u> 时，谢瓦利埃小姐 <u> 打断 </u> 了我，问我是否知道“impetuous”这个词的意思。 <u> 尽管 </u> 她带着 <u> 鼓励的 </u> 微笑，但我还是想找个 <u> 地 </u> 缝 <u> 钻 </u> 进去，因为我 <u> 不确定 </u> 这个词的 <u> 发音 </u> ，也不知道它的 <u> 意思 </u> 。谢瓦利埃小姐 <u> 假装 </u> 没有 <u> 注意到 </u> 我涨 <u> 红 </u> 的脸， <u> 递给 </u> 我一本词典，让我 <u> 大声 </u> 读出它的 <u> 释义 </u> 。“impetuous有两个释义：以极大的 <u> 力量 </u> 或 <u> 暴力猛冲 </u> ；不假思索地突然行动。”

paragraphs.en: She asked me which one fitted the poem.I read {both} definitions over again, trying to figure it out, but Miss Chevalier must have read my {mind}.“There is no {wrong} answer,”she said,“I want to know your opinion, Addie.” {hesitantly}, I said,“ {maybe}...both.”
paragraphs.cn: 她问我哪个释义适合这首诗。我把 <u> 两个 </u> 释义又 <u> 都 </u> 读了一遍，试图弄清楚，但谢瓦利埃小姐一定是看穿了我的 <u> 心思 </u> ，她说：“没有 <u> 错误的 </u> 答案，我只想知道你的看法，艾迪。”我 <u> 犹豫了一下 </u> ，说：“ <u> 也许 </u> ……两个都适合。”

paragraphs.en: She liked that.“One has to be impetuous both ways or they wouldn't {dare} to face up to any {challenge}.Would you call {yourself} impetuous?”
paragraphs.cn: 她喜欢这个回答。“一个人必须有这两种冲动，否则就不会 <u> 敢于 </u> 面对任何 <u> 挑战 </u> 。你觉得 <u> 你自己 </u> 冲动吗？”

paragraphs.en: I knew she was asking for an opinion.“My {mother} thinks being impetuous for girls is {improper}, {anyway}.”
paragraphs.cn: 我知道她想听听我的看法。“ <u> 不管怎样 </u> ，我 <u> 妈妈 </u> 觉得女孩冲动是 <u> 不妥当的 </u> 。”

paragraphs.en: She said my mom was {somewhat} right about that.“But girls should also be {wise} to take up challenges when needed.I {believe} you are such a girl.”
paragraphs.cn: 她说我妈妈说得 <u> 有几分 </u> 道理。“但女孩也应该在需要时 <u> 明智 </u> 地接受挑战。我 <u> 相信 </u> 你就是这样的女孩。”
